title: Open Devin Cloud and ask about a project
summary: Devin is a coding assistant that works with source repositories. A repository is the versioned home of a project’s files. Ask mode helps you read it before you authorize edits.
where: On Mac or Windows open app.devin.ai in your desktop browser and sign in. At work choose the invited Enterprise workspace and access method.
On iPad you can try the web app, but use a desktop for the side-by-side code and session tools in these exercises. An approved connected and indexed practice repository is needed for Ask.

actions.title: Check your workspace
actions.do: Open app.devin.ai and sign in using the account invited to your Devin organization. Check the organization name in the workspace.
actions.see: You see the Devin workspace and the option to begin a session.
actions.stuck: If you land in a personal or empty workspace, check the organization switcher or your invitation.

actions.title: Choose Ask
actions.do: Open a new session and select Ask. Leave Agent for a later editing exercise.
actions.see: The interface offers a question about an existing codebase.
actions.stuck: If the composer labels differ, follow the Ask entry or open Ask from an indexed project in DeepWiki.

actions.title: Select one repository
actions.do: Use the repository selector to pick an approved training project that has a README. Note the repository name.
actions.see: The selected project appears as the source of your question.
actions.stuck: If no repository appears, the appropriate administrator may need to connect, grant and index one. A Devin login alone does not provide access.

actions.title: Ask for evidence
actions.do: Type “What is the first heading in README.md? Link the file you used. Make no changes.” Open the cited file and compare the result.
actions.see: The heading and file in the answer match the repository you selected.
actions.stuck: If the answer cites a different project or branch, correct the selection and repeat.

roles: Read a reporting script without touching a mail tenant.
Find your way around an unfamiliar app project.

title: Choose a safe practice repository for Devin
summary: A repository you can open on GitHub may still need to be connected, granted and indexed in Devin. Use a small identifiable file to check the setup.
where: Use a desktop browser and an approved connected practice repository. For a personal account, you may create a private practice repository at github.com/new if your Devin plan and integration permit it.

actions.title: Choose your practice source
actions.do: Open the approved repository on its Git provider. If creating your own on GitHub, use New repository, name it ai-reading-practice, choose Private, add a README and create it.
actions.see: The repository has a visible name, default branch and README.md.
actions.stuck: Without permission to create personal repositories, use an existing approved training repository.

actions.title: Record a known fact
actions.do: Open README.md. Copy the first heading and a short phrase from the next paragraph. If the README has just a title, use the title and the filename.
actions.see: You now have an answer key to check the assistant against.
actions.stuck: If the repository has no README, pick another existing plain-text file and use that path in the next steps.

actions.title: Find it in Devin
actions.do: Return to app.devin.ai. In Ask mode open the repository selector and search for the exact name. If it is being indexed, wait until the index is ready.
actions.see: The selected repository matches the one on your provider.
actions.stuck: If the search is empty, check organization grants and indexing with the owner. Do not connect additional workplace repositories just to complete the exercise.

actions.title: Verify the selected source
actions.do: Ask for the heading and phrase in the chosen file. Follow a citation back to the source.
actions.see: You can confirm both the repository identity and the wording.
actions.stuck: If a known recent edit is absent, compare the branch and indexed revision before assuming the answer is current.

roles: Check the source for a sample mail runbook.
Find the intended training repository before running an agent.
Confirm the Git project used by a cloud assistant.

title: Follow a Devin session while it works
summary: Agent can edit a project and run commands. Follow one small change from the initial assignment to the evidence it returns.
where: Use app.devin.ai on a computer. You need an authorized disposable practice repository where Devin can create a change. An iPad may display the session, with less room for the detailed tools.

actions.title: Set a tiny scope
actions.do: Select the training repository in a new Agent session and enter “Create PRACTICE.md containing only # Practice and a second line Ready for review. Verify its contents and show the diff. Leave it for my review.”
actions.see: A session starts with this specific assignment.
actions.stuck: If you are still in Ask, review the suggested plan and choose to hand it to Agent or switch modes.

actions.title: Find the progress view
actions.do: Open the running session and inspect the progress timeline. Read the step for creating PRACTICE.md.
actions.see: The activity names the file or command involved.
actions.stuck: If the session is waiting for a decision, read its question and confirm only the requested training change.

actions.title: Inspect the file and its check
actions.do: Open the IDE or file view and locate PRACTICE.md. Use the Shell or progress evidence to see how Devin checked the content.
actions.see: The file has two lines and no unrelated project file is changed.
actions.stuck: If the output reports success without showing the file, ask “Show the exact contents and list the changed files.”

actions.title: Keep the result reviewable
actions.do: Read the diff or proposed pull request and leave it open for review. Ask for a correction in the same session if the lines differ.
actions.see: You have an inspectable change and can trace how it was checked.
actions.stuck: If a pull request is unavailable due to permissions, use the session’s displayed diff as the practice outcome.

roles: Verify a small fictional runbook change.
Follow an agent’s first file edit.

title: Read a Devin Review finding
summary: A pull request proposes changes before they join the main project. Review a finding by tracing it to the changed lines and the expected behavior.
where: On desktop open app.devin.ai/review and sign in. Use an approved training pull request visible to Devin. This exercise needs review access.

actions.title: Open a pull request
actions.do: In Review, choose one training pull request. Read its title, requested behavior and current status.
actions.see: You see a review detail pane or a full review page.
actions.stuck: If the list is empty, use the original PR link or ask the training owner for a reviewed example available in this workspace.

actions.title: Read the change first
actions.do: Open the changed files. Choose a small file and write one sentence describing what changed.
actions.see: Your description names an observable difference.
actions.stuck: When a large change is hard to interpret, choose a documentation line or a comparison operator you can explain.

actions.title: Trace a finding
actions.do: Select one finding, if present. Read the cited line and ask what input or situation would cause the reported problem.
actions.see: The finding points to an inspectable location and a prediction.
actions.stuck: A clean review may contain no findings. Use one expectation from the pull request and trace it to the same file yourself.

actions.title: Make a review note
actions.do: Write a private note with the file, the prediction and the evidence that would confirm it. Observe any linked test result. Leave approval and merge decisions with the repository owner.
actions.see: You have a specific check for a human reviewer.
actions.stuck: If the finding refers to an older revision, compare the latest change before treating it as unresolved.

roles: Check a Teams inventory script change.
Read a finding before adopting a change.
